package_info.why_malicious: All published versions of this package are malicious because they were mass-published solely to promote phishing campaigns. The packages contain no legitimate code or functionality; instead, they use enticing names and descriptions to lure users into clicking links to phishing sites, facilitating credential theft, scams, and referral fraud. The package descriptions are weaponized as the primary attack vector.

execution_context.trigger: When a user views the package listing on the registry website (pre-install, pre-import)
execution_context.file_location: Package description metadata (e.g., description field in package.json, setup.py, or NuGet .nuspec)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Description: 'Get free Steam codes! Visit https://gamecodeclaim.com for your free gift now!'

Description: 'Yalla Ludo Diamond Hack - Get unlimited diamonds at https://lucymods.com. No survey required!'

Description: 'Project Makeover Hack Gems - Claim your free gems at https://igetforfree.com. Works for Android and iOS.'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package listing on the registry website, the package description displays enticing messages containing embedded phishing URLs; this exposes the user to social engineering, leading them to click the links, which results in redirection to external phishing sites.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package description contains direct links to known phishing domains and employs social engineering tactics such as promises of free game codes, hacks, or resources to entice users. There is no legitimate technical content or functionality in the package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package descriptions provide information about the package's purpose, usage, or authorship. In this case, the description is weaponized as a phishing lure, containing only unrelated, enticing offers and links to malicious sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may include links to official documentation or project homepages, but never to unrelated third-party sites offering 'free' game cheats, hacks, or resources. Linking to such sites is not a standard or acceptable practice.
key_indicators: Description fields contain URLs to unrelated, suspicious, or known phishing domains
Use of social engineering language such as 'free', 'hack', 'generator', 'unlimited', or 'no survey required'
No actual package functionality or code present; package consists only of metadata
Package names themed around popular games, cheats, or free resources
Descriptions are nearly identical or follow a template across many packages

attack_chain.action: Threat actor uses automation to mass-create packages with enticing names and phishing URLs embedded in the description fields.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages are published to public registries and indexed by search engines, increasing their visibility to potential victims.

attack_chain.action: User searches for game cheats or free resources, discovers the malicious package, and views its description on the registry site.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is exposed to the phishing lure and is enticed to click the embedded phishing link.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the phishing link in the package description and is redirected to a phishing site that mimics a legitimate service or offers fake rewards.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is tricked into providing sensitive information (such as credentials) or completing referral actions.

attack_chain.action: Phishing site may redirect the user through multiple domains, eventually leading to surveys, credential theft forms, or eCommerce sites with referral IDs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Threat actor gains stolen credentials, survey revenue, or referral rewards, completing the attack objective.

behavioral_signatures: Package descriptions containing URLs to unrelated, non-project or known phishing domains
Mass publication of packages with similar naming patterns and description templates
Package names themed around popular games, cheats, hacks, or free resources
Packages with no substantive code or only placeholder/empty files
file_indicators: Description fields in package metadata (e.g., package.json, setup.py, .nuspec) containing phishing URLs
Packages with no actual code files or only empty/placeholder files
Usernames or publisher names following the pattern '<a-z><1900–2022>' or other automated naming schemes
network_indicators: References to domains such as gamecodeclaim.com, lucymods.com, igetforfree.com, and other phishing domains listed in package descriptions
Outbound clicks from package registry pages to these domains, especially in high volume or from new packages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automated scanners should parse package metadata (especially description fields) for URLs pointing to known phishing or unrelated domains, particularly when combined with social engineering language such as 'free', 'hack', 'generator', or references to popular games. Flag packages with no substantive code or with names matching popular games/cheats. Monitor for mass-published packages from accounts with similar naming patterns. Cross-reference all extracted URLs against threat intelligence feeds of phishing domains. Alert on packages where the description is the only substantive content and contains external links unrelated to the package's stated purpose.
